description: Searchable rules entries for ordinary, historical, supernatural, future, scavenged, survival, and alien equipment. Canonical item records remain in the linked rules catalogs.

entries.title: Equipment Foundation
entries.summary: Equipment uses a compact record: attack or activation, damage or Armor Rating, range, Load, tags, uses, requirements, and limitations.
body: Equipment is an external capability source. It grants only the function, protection, damage, range, tag, use, and permission printed in its record. A recognizable name, expensive construction, historical reputation, alien material, supernatural appearance, or improvised origin grants nothing beyond that record.

Weapons use the existing Simple Combat procedure. After a hit, roll printed Damage Dice; firearm critical successes add damage dice. Armor Rating adds eligible soak dice. Ordinary Armor never soaks Aggravated damage. Relics and alien systems follow the same capability-first requirement as Archetype abilities.

Load gives Carry a direct purpose without adding a second encumbrance subsystem. Carry total Load up to Carry normally. Each point above Carry subtracts one die from Athletics and Mobility, to a maximum of three dice, and prevents Sprinting.
Catalog statistics assume Serviceable condition. Damaged equipment creates an extra equipment Complication on its first failed use each scene, and Damaged armor loses one Armor Rating until repaired.

entries.title: Modern Arms and Armor
entries.summary: Thirty-four modern weapons and twelve modern armor or protective systems using generic categories rather than brand-specific models.
body: The modern catalog covers impact weapons, knives and breaching tools, less-lethal devices, pistols, compact automatic weapons, shotguns, carbines, rifles, machine guns, anti-materiel weapons, launchers, grenades, flamethrowers, bows, and crossbows.

The armor catalog includes reinforced clothing, soft and hard ballistic vests, plate carriers, riot armor, helmets, shields, bomb suits, fire-entry protection, hazardous-material suits, tactical environmental suits, and industrial powered exoskeletons.

The catalog deliberately uses role categories rather than commercial model names. A particular real-world model can normally use the nearest generic record unless a campaign needs a meaningful difference.

entries.title: World War and Medieval Equipment
entries.summary: Short, functional catalogs for World War I, World War II, and medieval arms and armor without replacing the modern baseline.
body: World War I includes a service revolver, bolt-action rifle, trench shotgun, bayonet, trench club, early light machine gun, stick grenade, and steel helmet.
World War II includes a service pistol, semi-automatic rifle, sniper rifle, submachine gun, light and heavy machine guns, flamethrower, anti-tank launcher, fragmentation grenade, and flak vest.

The medieval catalog includes common one-handed and two-handed weapons, polearms, bows, crossbows, padded armor, leather, mail, brigandine, full plate, and shields. Historical armor remains ordinary Armor and never becomes supernatural protection through age or craftsmanship alone.

entries.title: Supernatural Artifacts and Relics
entries.summary: Twenty-two original relics whose supernatural effects require exact wielders, Skills, attunement, costs, limits, and failures.
body: Relics are not universal magic items. Anyone may carry, steal, hide, study, damage, or sell one, but its supernatural capability functions only for a character who meets every Wielder Requirement and Skill Requirement and completes its Attunement.

The catalog includes consecrated anti-undead instruments, vampiric blood-memory objects, lunar weapons and mantles, Eldritch Binder restraints, Harmonic resonance devices, Technomancer analytical lenses, identity defenses, memorial instruments, temporal devices, relationship relics, and survival sanctuaries.

Aggravated damage is always target-specific. The Ashen Sun Reliquary affects only blood-fed undead and exact cursed-solar vulnerabilities; the Moon-Silver Fang affects only its explicitly named corrupted or crisis targets; the Executioner's Mercy requires a separate recorded supernatural judgment capability.

entries.title: Future Weapons, Armor, and Systems
entries.summary: Sixteen human-compatible future weapons and eighteen armor, medical, sensor, fabrication, drone, and interface systems.
body: Future technology remains ordinary equipment unless it explicitly invokes Disruption, identity control, phase behavior, or another defined capability. A plasma cutter is dangerous and technologically advanced but still deals ordinary Lethal damage unless a separate rule makes it Aggravated.

Weapons include coil and flechette systems, pulse rifles, arc projectors, plasma tools, particle lances, gravitic control weapons, monofilament and phase-edged melee systems, sonic disruptors, microdrone clouds, breach foam, and identity-scrambler darts.

Support equipment includes smartweave and powered armor, vacuum combat suits, kinetic shielding, identity firewalls, adaptive camouflage, field fabricators, med-gel, regeneration cocoons, repair swarms, drones, grav sleds, translation lattices, noospheric isolation, multispectrum scanning, and universal interface frames.

tables.title: Future Weapon Baselines
rows: AP 2; damages its housing on a Complication
Suppresses false credentials and remote identity access

entries.title: Scavenged and Improvised Equipment
entries.summary: Twenty salvage and field-built records with useful functions and explicit breakdown, exposure, or maintenance consequences.
body: Scavenged equipment is usually Damaged until repaired. Improvised construction grants a specific field function, not an open-ended permission to invent whatever is convenient during the scene.

The catalog includes pipe and scrap firearms, reclaimed energy weapons, scrap melee arms, shock prods, industrial nail drivers, cutting torches, improvised flame projectors and charges, salvage shields, patched pressure suits, respirators, jammers, alarms, barricades, cable launchers, utility drones, medical kits, battery banks, and sealant rigs.

Every dangerous improvised device has a bounded failure. The jury-rigged flame projector can rupture; the shock prod can discharge through its wielder; the reclaimed pulse weapon can inflict Disruption; the patched pressure suit loses its seal when penetrating damage gets through.

tables.title: Scavenged Gear Examples
rows: Any attack die showing 1 empties it

-2 dice to unsecured wireless systems in 10 meters

Temporary suit, pipe, container, or hull seal

entries.title: Survival and Expedition Gear
entries.summary: Thirty-four practical medical, shelter, air, water, navigation, climbing, repair, evidence, sanitation, and recovery records.
body: Survival gear establishes permission and bounded bonuses for field care, shelter, movement, contamination control, navigation, communication, repair, sample preservation, and sustained operation. It does not erase the need for Skills, time, supplies, or an environment containing the resource being sought.

The catalog includes first-aid, trauma, and surgery kits; rations, water purification, shelter, heat, respiratory and pressure protection; radiation detection and shielding; climbing, flotation, navigation, signals, optics, lights, repair supplies, power cells, foraging, evidence collection, body recovery, and sanitation.
Specialized biology, alien chemistry, supernatural contamination, and unknown radiation require an explicit compatible item or a successful test establishing that ordinary equipment applies.

entries.title: Alien Technology Templates
entries.summary: Sixteen overlays for converting a base weapon, armor item, tool, vehicle component, medical system, archive, or habitat into explicit alien technology.
body: Alien technology templates answer five questions: what type of base item can carry the template, how the interface works, what translation is required, what bounded benefit it produces, and how it becomes unstable or fails.

The templates include Ar'nock biofabrication, noospheric credential locks, symbiotic organisms, gravitic inversion, phase displacement, crystalline resonance, null fields, memory-reactive material, modular swarms, probability bias, temporal latency, ecological integration, identity-responsive control, folded thresholds, archive organisms, and causal permission machines.

A template does not make an item generically superior. It changes only named fields and introduces a real interface or failure problem. Reverse engineering can reveal facts and reproduce bounded functions, but it cannot silently create unique materials, manufacturing infrastructure, living trust, alien authority, or supernatural personhood.
